title: What Ice Sheet Early Warning Is
definition: Ice Sheet Early Warning: warning systems for ice collapse.
description:

t: 2030 — First governed warning hulls field trials: warning logistics mon
title: 2030 — First governed warning hulls field trials: warning logistics mon
definition: 2030 milestone on the Ice Sheet Early Warning roadmap.
description:
First governed warning hulls field trials: warning logistics monitoring published openly, sea-level models oversight in place.

What must be true first: the ice sensors results have to replicate outside the lab, warning logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and sea-level models operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed ice sensors demonstrations, warning logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting sea-level models uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

t: Readiness Estimator: Ice Sheet Early Warning
title: Readiness Estimator: Ice Sheet Early Warning
definition: Estimates Ice Sheet Early Warning readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Ice Sheet Early Warning components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a warning hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

t: Ice Sheet Early Warning Systems Simulator
title: Ice Sheet Early Warning Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Ice Sheet Early Warning operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Ice Sheet Early Warning installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 39401 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where ice sensors monitoring, warning logistics redundancy, or sea-level models maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

t: Ice Sheet Early Warning Master Roadmap
title: Ice Sheet Early Warning Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Ice Sheet Early Warning: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Ice Sheet Early Warning — warning systems for ice collapse.

Phase 1 — Prove (ice sensors): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (warning logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (sea-level models): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (evacuation plans): warning hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and polar-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
